name: slots.expressionFocus

name: slots.courseSpecifics
description: The pupils are Norwegian teenagers in Years 8–10 of lower secondary school, learning English as a second language: most have Norwegian as their first language, and some have another home language. Teach and practise in English, at a level that suits second-language learners, and point out where Norwegian habits lead them astray; a word of Norwegian is fine to clear up a misunderstanding. After Year 10 a pupil can be drawn for a centrally set written exam (five hours, digital, no preparation day, with parts on listening and reading, relaying content, written interaction and a longer text of their own) or for a locally set oral exam with a preparation part.

name: Plan your own language learning
description: set a concrete goal for your English, choose ways of practising that fit it, such as reading, watching series with English subtitles or speaking, and judge afterwards whether it worked.

name: Work out the meaning of an unknown word
description: work out what an unfamiliar word means from the context, from its prefix or suffix and from similar words in Norwegian, and check the guess in a dictionary.

name: Look up a word in a dictionary
description: find the right meaning of a word in an English or English–Norwegian dictionary, using its word class, the example sentences and the pronunciation given.

name: Use digital aids critically
description: use spell-check, online dictionaries and translation tools without letting them choose for you, and spot the errors they typically make, such as picking the wrong meaning of a word with several senses.

name: Keep talking when you lack a word
description: get round a missing word by describing it, using a more general word or giving an example, instead of stopping or switching to Norwegian.

name: Cognate and false friend
description:
Cognate: a word that looks similar and means the same in two languages, like water and vann.
False friend: a word that looks like a word in another language but means something different, like eventually, which means til slutt and not eventuelt.

name: Common false friends
description:
eventually: til slutt (not eventuelt)
actually: faktisk (not aktuelt)
sensible: fornuftig (not sensibel)
novel: roman (a novelle is a short story)
chef: kokk (not sjef)
become: bli (not bekomme)
gift: gave (the Norwegian gift means married or poison)
rare: sjelden (not rar)
brave: modig (not brav)
fabric: stoff (not fabrikk)
sympathetic: medfølende (not sympatisk)

name: Compare English with Norwegian or another language you know
description: point out similarities and differences between English and Norwegian, or another language you know, in words, word order and grammar, and use them to avoid typical mistakes.

name: Word stress and sentence stress
description:
Word stress: the syllable in a word that is said louder and longer, as in PHOtograph and phoTOgraphy.
Sentence stress: the words in a sentence that carry the meaning and are stressed, while small words like a, the and of are said weakly.

name: Intonation
description: Intonation: the rise and fall of the voice across a sentence, which signals for example whether it is a question, a statement or a list.

name: English sounds that differ from Norwegian
description:
th in think: voiceless, tongue between the teeth (not t)
th in this: voiced, tongue between the teeth (not d)
w in wet: rounded lips, no teeth (not v)
v in very: upper teeth on the lower lip (not w)
z in zoo: a voiced, buzzing s; Norwegian has no such sound
j in jam: the sound in edge (not the Norwegian j)
sh in ship and s in sip: two different sounds that keep words apart

name: Pronounce English clearly
description: pronounce English so that a listener understands you without effort, with the right word stress, the th, w, v and z sounds, natural sentence stress, and intonation that rises and falls in the right places.

name: Variety of English
description: Variety of English: a form of English used in one region or group, with its own pronunciation, words and sometimes grammar, such as British, American, Australian, Indian or Nigerian English. No variety is more correct than another.

name: British and American words
description:
lift: elevator
flat: apartment
autumn: fall
football: soccer
trousers: pants
pavement: sidewalk
biscuit: cookie
mobile phone: cell phone
holiday: vacation
rubbish: garbage or trash
queue: line
petrol: gas
colour, centre, organise (British spelling): color, center, organize (American spelling)

name: Listen for the main point
description: listen to a conversation, interview or report and say what it is mainly about and what the speakers think.

name: Listen for specific information
description: listen for particular details, such as a name, a number, a reason or an opinion, and choose the answer that matches what was actually said, not one that merely sounds similar.

name: Understand speakers of different varieties of English
description: follow speakers with different accents and varieties of English, and recognise some typical features of British, American and at least one other variety.

name: Word classes
description: Word class: a group of words that behave the same way in a sentence. The main ones in English are noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction and determiner, which includes the articles a, an and the.

name: Prefix and suffix
description:
Prefix: a part added to the start of a word that changes its meaning, such as un-, dis-, re- and im-.
Suffix: a part added to the end of a word that often changes its word class, such as -ness, -ment, -ful and -ly.

name: Subject, verb and object
description:
Subject: the person or thing that does the action or is described, usually before the verb.
Verb: the word or words that say what happens or what something is.
Object: the person or thing the action is done to.

name: English word order
description: English word order: subject, then verb, then object in a statement. The subject stays before the verb even when the sentence starts with a time or place expression: Yesterday I went home, not Yesterday went I home.

name: Do in questions and negatives
description: Do-support: in questions and negatives with a main verb and no other helping verb, English adds do, does or did: Do you like it? She doesn't know. Did they come?

name: Write sentences with correct word order
description: write statements, questions and negative sentences with English word order, also when the sentence starts with a time or place expression, and put adverbs like often and never before the main verb.

name: Subject–verb agreement
description: Subject–verb agreement: the verb matches its subject in number, so in the present simple she plays but they play, and a singular word like everyone, nobody or each takes a singular verb.

name: Make the verb agree with the subject
description: add -s or -es to the verb in the present simple when the subject is he, she, it or one person or thing, use does and doesn't in questions and negatives, and get agreement right in longer sentences.

name: Present simple and present continuous
description:
Present simple: for habits, facts and states: I play football on Mondays.
Present continuous: am, is or are plus -ing, for something going on now or around now: I am playing football right now.

name: Past simple and present perfect
description:
Past simple: a finished action at a finished time, often with a time expression: I saw it yesterday.
Present perfect: have or has plus the past participle, linking the past to now, with no finished time: I have seen it.

name: Common irregular verbs
description:
be: was/were, been
go: went, gone
see: saw, seen
take: took, taken
write: wrote, written
know: knew, known
think: thought, thought
buy: bought, bought
bring: brought, brought
catch: caught, caught
teach: taught, taught
begin: began, begun
drink: drank, drunk
swim: swam, swum
eat: ate, eaten
fall: fell, fallen
feel: felt, felt
find: found, found
give: gave, given
leave: left, left
choose: chose, chosen
throw: threw, thrown
speak: spoke, spoken
rise: rose, risen
lie (ligge): lay, lain
lay (legge): laid, laid

name: Ways to talk about the future
description:
Will: for predictions and for decisions made as you speak: I think it will rain. I'll help you.
Going to: for plans, and for something you can see coming: I'm going to study tonight.
Present continuous: for fixed arrangements: We're meeting at six.

name: Choose the right tense
description: choose between present simple and present continuous, between past simple and present perfect, and between the future forms, and keep the tenses consistent through a text.

name: Countable and uncountable nouns
description:
Countable noun: something that can be counted and has a plural: a book, two books.
Uncountable noun: something treated as a mass, with no plural and no a or an, such as information, advice, furniture, news and homework.

name: Articles
description:
Indefinite article: a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound (a university, an hour), used with one countable thing.
Definite article: the, used for something specific or already mentioned. English uses no article for things in general: Dogs are loyal. Life is short.

name: Use articles and plurals correctly
description: use a, an, the or no article, and choose between much and many and between little and few, for countable and uncountable nouns.

name: Adjective and adverb
description:
Adjective: describes a noun: a quick answer.
Adverb: describes a verb, an adjective or a whole sentence, often formed with -ly: She answered quickly. Good is the adjective and well the adverb.

name: Relative pronoun
description: Relative pronoun: a word that starts a clause describing a noun: who for people, which for things, that for both, and whose for possession, as in the boy who won and the book which I read.

name: Words that sound alike
description:
its: belonging to it (its colour)
it's: it is or it has
their: belonging to them
there: in that place, or in there is and there are
they're: they are
your: belonging to you
you're: you are
whose: belonging to whom
who's: who is or who has
then: after that
than: in comparisons (bigger than)
to: towards, or before a verb (to go)
too: also, or more than enough
lose: miste or tape
loose: løs

name: Combine clauses into longer sentences
description: join clauses with conjunctions and relative pronouns to write varied sentences, and avoid run-on sentences where two sentences are glued together with only a comma.

name: Capital letters in English
description:
I: always a capital letter
days and months: Monday, July
nationalities and languages: Norwegian, English
titles of books and films: the main words get capitals (The Hunger Games)
names of people, places and organisations: capitals, as in Norwegian

name: Use English punctuation
description: use full stops, commas, apostrophes and quotation marks the English way: no comma before that, a comma after an introductory phrase, and apostrophes for possession (the girl's bag, the girls' bags) and for contractions (don't).

name: Spell words with endings correctly
description: spell words that change when an ending is added: double consonants (stop, stopped), a dropped e (make, making), y to i (happy, happier; study, studies), and plurals with -es (box, boxes).

name: Find and correct grammar errors in your own text
description: go through your own text for the typical errors, such as a missing -s in the third person, the wrong tense, its and it's, word order and capital letters, and correct them.

name: Formal and informal register
description:
Register: the level of formality in language, chosen to fit purpose, recipient and situation.
Formal: full forms, polite phrases and precise words, as in a job application.
Informal: contractions, everyday words and slang, as in a message to a friend.

name: Idiom
description: Idiom: a fixed expression whose meaning cannot be worked out from the individual words, like it's raining cats and dogs or break the ice.

name: Collocation
description: Collocation: words that naturally go together in English, like make a mistake (not do a mistake), take a photo, heavy rain and strong coffee.

name: Common idioms
description:
a piece of cake: very easy
break the ice: make people feel relaxed when they first meet
once in a blue moon: very rarely
under the weather: slightly ill
cost an arm and a leg: be very expensive
on the fence: undecided
the ball is in your court: it is your turn to decide or act
spill the beans: reveal a secret
get cold feet: become nervous and want to back out
hit the books: study hard

name: Common phrasal verbs
description:
give up: stop trying
find out: discover
look after: take care of
look forward to: be happy about something that is coming
put off: postpone
turn down: refuse, or lower the volume
run out of: have no more left
come up with: think of an idea
get along with: have a good relationship with
carry on: continue

name: Vary your vocabulary
description: replace overused words like good, nice, bad, thing and a lot with more precise ones, and use idioms, phrasal verbs and collocations where they fit.

name: Adapt your language to purpose, recipient and situation
description: choose words, phrases and level of formality to suit who you are speaking or writing to and why, and rewrite a short text from informal to formal or the other way round.

name: Polite phrases
description:
asking for something: Could I have …? / Would you mind …?
interrupting: Sorry to interrupt, but …
disagreeing: I'm not sure I agree, because …
asking someone to repeat: Sorry, could you say that again?
apologising: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to …
thanking: Thank you so much, I really appreciate it.

name: Talk about a topic for a few minutes
description: talk without a script about a familiar topic for two to three minutes, in a clear order, with linking words and few long pauses.

name: Ask follow-up questions
description: keep a conversation going by asking open questions and following up on what the other person says, with phrases like What do you mean by …? and Why do you think so?

name: Take part in a discussion
description: give your opinion with a reason, agree and disagree politely, and respond to what the others actually said, with phrases like I see your point, but …

name: Give a prepared oral presentation
description: give a presentation with a clear introduction, main part and conclusion, speak from keywords rather than reading a script, and adapt it to your audience.

name: Answer questions about your own presentation
description: answer unprepared questions about your topic, explain the choices you made, and develop your answers beyond a sentence, as in an oral exam conversation.

name: Skim and scan a text
description: skim a text to find its topic and main point, and scan it quickly for a particular piece of information.

name: Read for detail and read between the lines
description: read a text closely enough to answer questions about its details, and work out what the writer means without saying it directly.

name: Fiction and factual text
description:
Fiction: invented stories, such as novels, short stories, poems and films.
Factual text: a text about real things, such as a news article, a report, an encyclopedia entry or an opinion piece.

name: Common factual genres
description:
News article: reports recent events, with the most important facts first.
Opinion piece: argues for a view, such as a letter to the editor, a comment or a blog post.
Report: presents facts about a topic in an organised and neutral way.

name: Summarise a text
description: retell the main content of a text briefly in your own words, leaving out details and your own opinion.

name: Relay the content of something you have heard or read
description: pass on the main points of a conversation, interview or text to someone who has not heard or read it, briefly, in your own words and adapted to that person.

name: Present and discuss a text you have chosen
description: present a fiction or factual text you have chosen yourself by saying what it is about, what kind of text it is and what you think of it, and discuss it with others.

name: Fact and opinion
description:
Fact: a claim that can be checked and shown to be true or false.
Opinion: what someone thinks or feels about something, which can be argued for but not proved.

name: Source
description: Source: where information comes from, such as a website, a book, an article, a video or a person. A reliable source is one you have good reason to trust.

name: Bias
description: Bias: a slant in how a text presents something, favouring one side, for example through which facts it includes or leaves out and through loaded words.

name: Assess how reliable a source is
description: judge whether a factual text can be trusted by checking who made it and why, when it was published, whether it gives evidence, and whether other sources agree.

name: Quote and paraphrase a source
description: use information from a source either as an exact quotation in quotation marks or as a paraphrase in your own words, and say where it comes from either way.

name: Plagiarism
description: Plagiarism: presenting someone else's words, ideas or images as your own, including copying, handing in a translated text, or handing in AI-written text without saying so.

name: Refer to your sources
description: refer to your sources in the text and in a list at the end, with author, title, website or publisher, date and link, so that a reader can find them.

name: Plot and climax
description:
Plot: the events of a story and how they are linked by cause and effect.
Climax: the turning point where the tension is at its highest.

name: Character and characterisation
description:
Character: a person in a story.
Characterisation: how the writer shows what a character is like, directly by describing them, or indirectly through what they say, do and think.

name: Setting
description: Setting: when and where a story takes place, and the atmosphere this creates.

name: Conflict
description: Conflict: the problem or struggle that drives a story, between characters, between a character and society or nature, or inside one character.

name: Narrator and point of view
description:
Narrator: the voice that tells the story.
First-person narrator: tells the story as I, from inside it.
Third-person narrator: tells it from outside, about he, she or they, and may know what one or all of the characters think.

name: Theme
description: Theme: the underlying idea a story explores, such as friendship, identity or prejudice. It is different from the plot, which is what happens.

name: Simile and metaphor
description:
Simile: a comparison using like or as: her eyes were like ice.
Metaphor: a comparison that says one thing is another: her eyes were ice.

name: Symbol
description: Symbol: a thing, place or event in a text that stands for something larger, like a locked door standing for a lost chance.

name: Short story, novel and young adult fiction
description:
Short story: a short piece of fiction, often with few characters, one main conflict, a sudden start and an open ending.
Novel: a long piece of fiction with room for several characters, settings and plot lines.
Young adult fiction: novels written for teenagers, usually with a teenage main character and themes like identity, friendship and growing up.

name: Stanza, rhyme and repetition
description:
Stanza: a group of lines in a poem, like a paragraph in prose.
Rhyme: words that end in the same sound, often at the ends of lines.
Repetition: words or lines that are repeated for effect.

name: Analyse a short story
description: describe the setting, characters, conflict, narrator and structure of a short story, and use quotations to show how the writer builds tension or meaning.

name: Analyse a poem or song lyric
description: describe what a poem or song lyric is about, how it is built, which images and sound effects it uses, and what they add.

name: Interpret the theme of a text
description: suggest what a story, poem or film is really about, and support your interpretation with examples from the text.

name: Reflect on a novel you have read
description: talk or write about a young adult novel you have read: what it is about, how it presents a theme, and how it relates to your own life or to the world today.

name: Write a text about a literary work
description: write a structured text that analyses and interprets a short story, poem or novel, with an introduction, quotations as evidence and a conclusion.

name: Linking words
description: Linking word: a word or phrase that shows how sentences or paragraphs relate: addition (also, furthermore), contrast (however, although), cause (because, since), result (therefore, as a result) and time (then, afterwards).

name: Paragraph and topic sentence
description:
Paragraph: a group of sentences about one main idea, marked with a new line.
Topic sentence: the sentence, usually the first, that states the main idea of the paragraph.

name: Introduction, main part and conclusion
description:
Introduction: presents the topic and catches the reader's interest.
Main part: develops the content in paragraphs, one main idea in each.
Conclusion: rounds off the text, for example by summing up or giving a final thought, without bringing in new arguments.

name: Write a well-structured paragraph
description: write a paragraph with a topic sentence, supporting sentences with examples, and a link to the next paragraph.

name: Descriptive, narrative, reflective and argumentative texts
description:
Descriptive text: shows what someone or something is like, appealing to the senses.
Narrative text: tells a story, real or invented, as a sequence of events.
Reflective text: explores a question or an experience from several sides and shows the writer's own thinking.
Argumentative text: tries to convince the reader of a view.

name: Claim, reason and counterargument
description:
Claim: the view the writer or speaker wants others to accept.
Reason: why the claim should be accepted.
Evidence: facts, examples or sources that back up the reason.
Counterargument: a reason for the opposite view, which the writer answers.

name: Read a writing task carefully and plan your text
description: work out what a writing task asks for, such as the text type, the recipient, the purpose and every part that must be answered, and plan the text to match.

name: Write a narrative text
description: write a story with a clear beginning, a turning point and an ending, using dialogue and description, and keep the narrator and the tense consistent.

name: Write a descriptive text
description: describe a person, place or experience so the reader can see, hear and feel it, with precise words, details for the senses and figurative language.

name: Write an argumentative text
description: argue for a view with a clear claim, reasons backed by evidence and an answer to at least one counterargument, in a text with an introduction and a conclusion.

name: Write a reflective text
description: explore a question from more than one angle, link it to your own experience and to what you have read, and arrive at a considered view of your own.

name: Write a formal email or letter
description: write a formal email or letter, such as an application or a complaint, with a suitable greeting, a clear purpose, polite phrases and a suitable ending.

name: Write an informal message or post
description: write an informal message, blog post or social-media post in a friendly tone and everyday language, without slipping into text-speak where it does not fit.

name: Respond in writing to what others have written
description: reply to a post, letter or comment by referring to what the other person said, giving your own view with reasons, and keeping the exchange going.

name: Multimodal text
description: Multimodal text: a text that combines writing with images, sound, video or layout, where each part adds to the meaning.

name: Create a multimodal text
description: make a text such as a presentation, poster or video in which words, images and sound support each other, and credit images and music you have not made yourself.

name: Revise your text based on feedback
description: use feedback from a teacher or classmate, together with what you know about English, to improve the content, structure and language of your own text, not just correct single errors.

name: Write a longer text under exam conditions
description: plan, write and proofread a longer text of your own within a time limit, answering every part of the task, with a title, a clear structure, varied language and sources referred to where you use them.

name: Lingua franca and world language
description:
Lingua franca: a common language used between people who have different first languages.
World language: a language used across many countries and continents in trade, science, the internet and popular culture. English is both today.

name: Explain how English became a world language
description: explain how British colonisation, and later the economic and cultural power of the United States, spread English across the world, and what that means for the variety of Englishes spoken today.

name: Loanword and domain loss
description:
Loanword: a word taken from one language into another, like weekend and nice in Norwegian.
Domain loss: when one language takes over a whole area of use, such as research or business, so that the local language is no longer used there.

name: Reflect on the role of English in Norway
description: give examples of where English is used in Norway, in school, work, media and gaming, and discuss what it means for you and for Norwegian, for example through loanwords and domain loss.

name: The United Kingdom, Great Britain and the British Isles
description:
Great Britain: the island with England, Scotland and Wales.
United Kingdom: the country made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
British Isles: the group of islands that includes Great Britain and Ireland.

name: Multicultural society and stereotype
description:
Multicultural society: a society where people with different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds live together.
Stereotype: a fixed, simplified idea about what a group of people is like.

name: Communication patterns
description:
Communication pattern: the unwritten rules for how people talk to each other in a culture, such as how direct to be, how much to say please and thank you, and when to make small talk.
Small talk: light conversation about safe topics, like the weather, to be friendly.

name: Describe ways of living in an English-speaking country
description: describe everyday life, values, communication and diversity in an English-speaking country or community, and avoid presenting a stereotype as the whole picture.

name: Indigenous peoples
description: Indigenous peoples: the descendants of those who lived in an area before others colonised or settled it, with their own languages, cultures and ties to the land.

name: Colonisation and assimilation
description:
Colonisation: when a foreign power takes control of an area and its people, settles there and rules it, often taking land and suppressing the local culture.
Assimilation: pressure on a minority to give up its own language and culture and take on those of the majority.

name: Assimilation through schooling
description: Assimilation through schooling: indigenous children sent to residential or boarding schools, often far from home, where they were taught only the majority language and culture and were discouraged or forbidden from using their own, as happened in Canada, the United States and Norway. In Australia, many Aboriginal children were taken from their families; they are called the Stolen Generations.

name: Indigenous peoples in English-speaking countries and Norway
description:
Australia: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
New Zealand: the Māori
United States: Native Americans, Alaska Natives and Native Hawaiians
Canada: First Nations, Inuit and Métis
Norway: the Sámi

name: Key events in indigenous history
description:
the Treaty of Waitangi between the British Crown and Māori chiefs: 1840
the Sámi Parliament in Norway opened: 1989
the Australian Prime Minister's apology to the Stolen Generations: 2008
the final report of Canada's Truth and Reconciliation Commission on residential schools: 2015
the report of Norway's Truth and Reconciliation Commission on Norwegianisation: 2023

name: Compare the situation of indigenous peoples
description: compare the history and present situation of an indigenous people in an English-speaking country with those of the Sámi in Norway, looking at land, language and recognition, and reflect on why the past still matters today.

name: Camera angle, close-up and soundtrack
description:
Camera angle: the position a scene is filmed from. A low angle makes someone look powerful, a high angle makes them look small.
Close-up: a shot of a face or object at close range, often to show feeling.
Soundtrack: the music and sound in a film, which sets the mood.

name: Analyse a film or series episode
description: describe how a film or series episode uses story, characters and film techniques to create meaning and mood.

name: Explore and present a cultural expression you like
description: choose a film, series, song, game or other cultural expression from the English-speaking world that you care about, present what it is about, and say what it shows about the culture it comes from.
